Initial request pathway

Tell us the need clearly and safely.

Use this page to prepare an initial request for education, skill, medical, care, disability, livelihood or shelter-related support.

This form is not an emergency service and submission does not guarantee funding. For any immediate threat to life or safety, contact the appropriate local emergency service first.
How requests are considered

Need first. Evidence next. Decision responsibly.

A concise initial request helps the Trust understand the situation without asking you to expose sensitive documents publicly.

1

Initial information

Share the need, location, urgency and estimated requirement.

2

Screening and acknowledgement

The Trust reviews whether the request aligns with its objects and available capacity.

3

Safe verification

If shortlisted, supporting records may be requested through an appropriate private channel.

4

Decision or referral

The Trust may support, partially support, seek a partner, refer to another service or explain why it cannot proceed.

Protect your identity: Do not enter Aadhaar, PAN, bank PIN, OTP, full medical records or document images in this initial message.

40-1,500 characters. Do not include ID numbers, passwords, OTPs or full medical records.

Request categories

What may fall within the Trust's objects.

Availability depends on programme stage, verification, funds, partners, location and legal or safeguarding requirements.

EDUCATION

Learning and skills

Guidance, learning access, vocational preparation, digital training and need-based educational support.

MEDICAL

Health support

Verified medical assistance, medicine access, camps, referrals or emergency-support coordination.

CARE

Children and elders

Nutrition, protection, shelter pathways, education, health and care coordination.

LIVELIHOOD

Work and self-reliance

Skill development, self-employment, rural enterprise, disability inclusion and agricultural pathways.

Fair review

What a request does - and does not - mean.

The Trust aims to respond with dignity and clarity while protecting limited charitable resources for verified, purpose-aligned needs.

Submission is not approvalNo funding or service is guaranteed by sending a form.
Verification may be requiredIdentity, need, cost and service-provider details may be checked privately.
Support can take different formsDirect assistance, material support, a partner referral or guidance may be considered.
No fee to submitDo not pay an intermediary simply to send an initial request.
Common questions

Before submitting.

Can someone submit for another person?

Yes, when you have their knowledge or lawful authority. Explain your relationship and protect their sensitive information.

Should I send documents immediately?

No. Begin with the form. If the request can be considered, the Trust can explain which records are needed and how to share them safely.

How quickly will support be provided?

Timing depends on urgency, verification, programme capacity, location, partners and available resources. The urgency selection helps triage; it is not a delivery guarantee.

What if the Trust cannot fund the request?

Where possible, the response may include guidance or a referral pathway. A referral also depends on the availability and criteria of the receiving organisation.
